picks.excerpt: Quanta explores thermodynamic computers — chips (from startups Normal Computing and Extropic) that harness thermal fluctuations and noise to compute, promising to run generative-AI algorithms with dramatically lower energy use, a physics-driven rethink of the hardware substrate underlying modern AI.
picks.rationale: Freshest pick (07-15) and highest novelty: a physics-of-computing rethink promising far lower energy for generative AI — computing sub-domain, distinct outlet.

picks.excerpt: Scientists at the GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences used artificial intelligence to detect previously hidden slow-slip ('silent') events on California's San Andreas Fault, finding these creeping fault movements are followed by measurably increased seismic activity — a new AI-enabled window into earthquake precursors.
picks.rationale: Concrete AI-enabled discovery in seismology — hidden slow-slip events as earthquake precursors — high-impact, distinct geophysics sub-domain.

picks.excerpt: North Carolina State University researchers built BINND (Binding and Interaction Neural Network for DNA), a deep-learning model trained on 144 million DNA sequence pairs that predicts which DNA strands bind to one another with 83.5% accuracy — at least 10% better than prior methods — with applications in DNA computing, data storage and diagnostics.
picks.rationale: New model with a clear accuracy gain (83.5%, +10% over prior) spanning genomics and DNA computing/storage — biology sub-domain; 2nd and final phys.org pick under the outlet cap.

picks.excerpt: Researchers at the University of Osaka trained an AI model on molecular-dynamics simulations to evaluate 16 structural descriptors and identify the most effective ways to distinguish water's two competing liquid states, helping pin down a hidden 'critical point' in supercooled water and clarifying the origin of water's anomalous properties.
picks.rationale: AI applied to a long-standing physical-chemistry puzzle (supercooled water's critical point) — adds a distinct materials/chemistry sub-domain and a 4th outlet.

picks.excerpt: As AI systems become embedded across physics research — from particle detection to materials discovery — Physics World examines the 'black box' problem: researchers increasingly struggle to understand how these models reach their conclusions, raising questions about whether science is entering an era of discoveries without full comprehension.
picks.rationale: Insight piece on how AI is reshaping the scientific method itself (interpretability of AI-driven physics) — credible outlet, physics-method angle that rounds out the sub-domain spread.
